subject: Ridgemark private cluster: compact footprint, nodepool sizing & storage constraints
messages:
From: Ridgemark Ops <ops@ridgemark.com>
To: markus_klein@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private cluster — compact footprint & storage constraints (initial)

Hi Markus,

We are kicking off Sprint Zero here at Ridgemark and need guidance for a compact on-prem Kubernetes deployment to run Redwood privately. Our site is one rack footprint (half-populated), planned hardware arriving in 3 weeks. Key constraints:
- Max 12 physical servers (2U each) in a single rack
- No cross-rack HA (single-site) but redundant PSUs and top-of-rack switch
- 10Gb LAN baseline; 40Gb available if we request additional NICs (budget-sensitive)
- Local NVMe available on some servers (960GB - 1.6TB), and a small SAN for archival
- We need to host models (~15TB active), ephemeral KV caches, and a control plane with etcd backups off-site

Questions:
1) Minimal control plane sizing you recommend for production-grade Redwood inference in a single-rack site?
2) How to split nodepools for GPU inference, CPU workers, and build artifacts given only 12 servers?
3) Best practice for storing model artifacts (local NVMe vs SAN vs NFS)?
4) Network requirements (MTU, bonding, BGP/NAT) for expected throughput of 3–6k qps on peak?
5) Any preflight evidence we should prepare for SOC-style review?

Can you and your ops team sketch a compact plan and call out any blockers we should surface to procurement/security?

Thanks,
Marcus (on behalf of the Ridgemark intake)

--
Sam Li
Platform Operations
Ridgemark Systems
From: markus_klein@redwood.com
To: Sam Li <ops@ridgemark.com>
Cc: neha_kapoor@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 10:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster — compact footprint & storage constraints (initial)

Sam — thanks for the clear constraints. High-level answers and a compact proposal below; I copied Neha and Marissa to get storage and delivery details. This is a short-format preflight so we can identify hard blockers quickly.

Summary recommendations (short):
- Control plane: 3 dedicated control-plane VMs/hosts (external etcd quorum 3 recommended). If host count prohibits, use 3 VMs on separate physical hosts with maintenance isolation.
- Nodepools (12-server example): 3 control-plane hosts (can be smaller), 6 inference workers (GPU-capable or CPU depending on models), 2 batch/sidecar workers (CPU-heavy), 1 shared infra (logging/monitoring).
- Storage: model-serving best on fast shared blockstore + node-local NVMe for KV cache and temp model unpacking. Do not store active model weights only on NFS unless backed by fast SAN and consistent IO.
- Network: prefer 40Gb for GPU nodes (if available). Use LACP bonding (2x10Gb = 20Gb) if 40Gb not possible. MTU 9000 for NVMe-over-RoCE and model transfers; BGP for multi-homed egress is optional but useful for predictable egress in single-rack topology.
- Security/evidence: KMS integration, audit logs for model pull, disk encryption on model storage, and snapshot retention policy.

Open questions (we need answers to size accurately):
Q1) How many GPU nodes (if any) will you actually install?
Q2) Planned SAN performance (IOPS/throughput) and whether it supports RWO block volumes with CSI?
Q3) Are you able to run vendor-supported CSI (Ceph, Portworx, or SAN CSI)?
Q4) Does procurement accept an extra 2x10Gb NIC purchase if 40Gb is not budgeted?
Q5) Any compliance windows for backups off-site (retention/geo)?

Neha — see storage sizing and PV recommendations below (feel free to edit). Marissa — Ops handoff checklist & sprint-zero artifacts to attach.

Next steps: I will prepare a compact node-fleet layout and a short sprint-zero checklist to hand to your on-site team. If nothing is blocking, propose a 30-min call tomorrow to finalize NIC and SAN choices.

Regards,
Markus Klein
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
From: neha_kapoor@redwood.com
To: markus_klein@redwood.com, Sam Li <ops@ridgemark.com>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Thu, 9 May 2029 11:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Private cluster — compact footprint & storage constraints (initial)

Sam/Markus — adding a pragmatic storage sizing and layout for the single-rack constraint. I kept the math conservative for model churn and snapshots.

Assumptions: ~15TB active models, 2x model snapshot retention (30 days), 20% headroom for unpacked artifacts and cache.

Recommended layout:
- Node-local NVMe: Use for KV cache and ephemeral unpacking. Recommend putting 1.6TB NVMe on each inference host (6 hosts => 9.6TB local NVMe total).
- Shared blockstore (SAN or Ceph): Host model weights and longer-lived artifacts as RWO or RWX depending on CSI. Provision 40TB usable to start (15TB active + snapshots + headroom). Use replication factor 2 (or erasure-coded cluster) if using software storage.
- Hot vs cold split: Serve models from SAN-mounted fast tier, keep frequently used shards cached on NVMe. Implement an LRU eviction policy at the runtime layer.
- Backup: Daily incremental snapshots for model volumes; weekly off-site full backups. Ensure snapshot cadence aligns with SOC/PCI-like requirements.
- IO patterns: Large sequential reads during cold loads (20–600 MB/s per node during model load). Small random writes for logging and checkpoints. Aim SAN to deliver 1–2 GB/s aggregated for whole rack during peak model swaps.

Implementation notes:
- CSI: Prefer our validated CSI driver (Redwood CSI) or Ceph CSI. NFS is acceptable only if backed by fast SAN and the NFS server is not the single point of failure.
- Encryption: At-rest encryption on SAN + LUKS on any local NVMe where models are cached.

Attachments: I attached a compact nodepool sizing sheet and the quick PV policy.

-Neha
Lead Infrastructure Engineer | Redwood Inference

Subject: Fwd: Private cluster — compact footprint & storage constraints (proposal and sprint-zero)

Sam — forwarding a one-page compact plan and the sprint-zero checklist we use for single-rack customers. Key ask: please confirm the NIC options per server (2x10Gb, 2x25Gb, or 1x40Gb) and whether procurement can allot two spare hosts for control-plane anti-affinity.

Proposal highlights (actionable):
- Recommended physical count: 3 control-plane hosts (can be 1U each), 5 inference workers (prefer 2 GPU-capable), 2 CPU workers for batch/monitoring, 1 infra node for logging + ingress, and 1 spare for maintenance = 12 total.
- If you only have 10 hosts, collapse infra and spare into a lightweight infra pod and run control-plane VMs across 3 remaining hosts.
- NVMe usage: place KV cache and model unpacking on NVMe; mount model volumes from SAN. We will push an init-job to pre-warm the cache for the top N models.
- CNI & routing: use Calico (BGP) with MTU 9000 where possible; enable ip-in-ip fallback if MTU cannot be changed.

Attachments included (stubs): ridgemark-sprint-zero-checklist.xlsx, nodepool-sizing-proposal.pdf, pv-policy-notes.md

Proposed next step: 30-min intake call today 16:00 PT to lock NIC and GPU counts. If that works, Marissa will open the delivery JIRA and add procurement checklist.

Thanks,
Markus

Markus/Neha/Marissa — thanks, this is very helpful and pragmatic. Quick answers inline:
- Q1: We will have 2 true GPU servers (each with 2x A40-equivalent), 6 CPU-only workers, and 4 small control/infra hosts available in first delivery (12 total).
- Q2: SAN is a Dell PowerStore with advertised 10 GB/s and supports RWO CSI; storage team will confirm IOPS this afternoon.
- Q3: We can install Ceph CSI if recommended; procurement prefers using vendor-supported drivers but open to your validated Redwood CSI.
- Q4: Procurement can add a 2x10Gb NIC per server (LACP) if 40Gb is above budget.
- Backups: We require 90-day retention for model snapshots.

We can take the 16:00 PT call — invite incoming. Please include the checklist and the JIRA template.

Appreciate the quick turnaround — Sam
